title: The Longest Text
tagline: His tomb holds the longest funerary inscription in ancient Egypt — a library in stone.

scenes.text: Thebes, c. 670 BCE. The Assyrian Empire has just invaded Egypt. In the Valley of the Nobles, a High Priest of Amun commissions a tomb unlike any other. Its walls will hold more written text than any tomb in the ancient world — a desperate act of preservation when the old order is crumbling.

scenes.speaker: Pediamenopet
scenes.text: Write it all. Every spell from the Book of the Dead. Every chapter of the Amduat. The Litany of Ra. The Book of Caverns. If the temples fall, if the priests are scattered, this tomb must be a library that the earth itself will keep safe.

challenge.instruction: Before a single spell is carved, the draughtsmen rule the walls into squares. Lay out the first figure on the grid.
challenge.fact: The tomb of Pediamenopet at Thebes (TT33) holds the largest collection of funerary texts in Egypt, drawn from the Pyramid Texts, the Coffin Texts, the Book of the Dead and the books of the underworld such as the Amduat.

scenes.text: The tomb of Pediamenopet at Luxor is the largest private tomb in Egypt. Its walls are covered in religious texts written in carefully carved hieroglyphs — compilations from dozens of sacred books. Scholars still have not fully cataloged everything inscribed within it.

scenes.speaker: Head Scribe
scenes.text: High Priest, the Assyrian soldiers have been seen near the temple precinct. Should we stop the work and conceal the tomb entrance?

challenge.instruction: Assyrian soldiers idle by the temple gate over a board scratched in the stone. Keep them at their game — and their eyes off the tomb — by beating them at it.
challenge.fact: Pediamenopet lived during the Late Period, a turbulent age of foreign invasions. His vast tomb was a monument so packed with sacred texts that no conqueror's curse could erase all of them. Scholars are still copying and translating them today.

scenes.speaker: Pediamenopet
scenes.text: Do not stop. Assyrians occupy the land — they cannot occupy the afterlife. These texts have guided the souls of Egyptians through death for a thousand years. As long as they survive, Egypt survives. The pen does not stop for the sword.

challenge.instruction: These texts guide the soul through death, and the Book of the Dead promises the blessed a game of senet in the hereafter. Win the game of passing.
challenge.fact: The Book of the Dead (more accurately 'Book of Coming Forth by Day') was a personal funerary guide. Spell 125, the Weighing of the Heart, was the most critical: the deceased's heart was weighed against the feather of Ma'at. A heart heavier than the feather — burdened by sins — was devoured by the monster Ammit.

scenes.text: Pediamenopet served as High Priest during one of Egypt's most vulnerable periods. Yet his instinct — to preserve knowledge in stone when institutions fail — proved exactly right. His tomb texts survived the Assyrian occupation, the Greek conquest, the Roman Empire, and twenty-six centuries of burial.

challenge.instruction: Every text in its place and none repeated: lay out the panels of spells on the wall before the carvers begin.
challenge.fact: Pediamenopet held the title Chief Lector Priest — the priest who read the sacred books aloud during the rituals — which may explain why his tomb became a library of sacred texts.

scenes.speaker: Pediamenopet
scenes.text: They say the Assyrians are invincible. Perhaps. But every empire ends. What I carve into this limestone will still be here when their empire is a memory. Knowledge is the only thing that outlasts conquest. Remember that, and nothing essential is ever truly lost.

challenge.instruction: What he carves into this limestone will outlast the Assyrians. Build the great gateway of his tomb course by course, the cornice last.
challenge.fact: Pediamenopet's tomb contains texts copied from sources spanning 2,000 years — from Old Kingdom pyramid texts to New Kingdom funerary literature. His scribes were the original archivists, assembling a complete library of the afterlife's instruction manual in one underground room.

scenes.speaker: Pediamenopet
scenes.text: The lesson is simple. Peseshet stands at Memphis and the Miracle has begun. Bring me onto the board, put a Priest at my side, and let us measure Belief against Belief.

challenge.instruction: Fight lesson 1 · First Duel. Deploy Pediamenopet to Memphis, add the Priest, then tap Pediamenopet and tap Peseshet to attack. Win one attack.
challenge.fact: In a Local Event every card at the location counts: Pediamenopet brings 9 Belief, the Priest adds +2 (or +4 beside a Great Person who shares that identity), and the higher total wins the attack. The loser returns to its owner's hand unless Kill mode is on.
